source_alignment.purpose: Test whether QA residuals can drive variation/evaluation/selective retention of retrieval policies. This is not a full HippoRAG reproduction and does not use live reader answers.

pre_reconstruction_method_priors.principle: Map a noisy surface representation into a canonical representation before comparing or retrieving.
Split a root task into subproblems whose interface entity composes the answer chain.
Preserve the working baseline and change one bounded component at a time.

variation.claim: Yes/no comparison questions with two named entities fail when retrieval covers one side only; force dual entity anchors and PPR evidence before reading.
variation.trigger: question starts with a binary auxiliary, contains 'and', and exposes at least two capitalized anchors
variation.expected_effect: Increase all-support recall on comparison questions without changing unrelated rows.
variation.risk: Overfitting to surface capitalization; gate requires no support or answer-coverage regression.

variation.claim: Entity-anchor questions can miss an obvious title page; preserve the strongest BM25 evidence and insert at most one exact title-anchor candidate into the tail of top-k.
variation.trigger: question exposes at least one capitalized anchor
variation.expected_effect: Improve supporting-title coverage while preserving BM25's highest-confidence passages.
variation.risk: Can still displace a useful fifth passage; gate requires heldout no-regression.

variation.claim: Wh-questions with a named anchor can miss the anchor page; explicitly bridge through exact title anchors.
variation.trigger: question is a wh-question and contains at least one capitalized anchor
variation.expected_effect: Recover missing bridge pages when BM25 locks onto answer-like text.
variation.risk: Can push already-complete BM25 evidence out of top-k; should be rejected if harms occur.

variation.claim: Pseudo-relevance feedback from the first BM25 passages can expand implicit bridge terms for multi-hop QA.
variation.expected_effect: Improve supporting-fact fraction on residual rows with incomplete evidence chains.
variation.risk: Top passage terms can amplify a wrong first hop; should be rejected if support-chain regressions appear.

variation.claim: Representation-transform priors from the pre-reconstruction notes apply to QA: convert possessive, quoted, and parenthesized surface mentions into canonical corpus-title candidates before ranking.
variation.trigger: question contains quoted/title-like, possessive, or parenthesized entity mentions
variation.expected_effect: Recover anchor pages that BM25 misses because the question surface form differs from the title.
variation.risk: Can over-rank generic title matches; retained only if exact heldout rows show no support or answer regression.

variation.claim: Decomposition/composition priors from the pre-reconstruction notes apply to multi-hop QA: first retrieve an anchor page, extract the role-labeled bridge entity from that page, then retrieve the bridge page.
variation.trigger: question asks a relation chain such as creator/performer/director/husband/father/mother/plaintiff
variation.expected_effect: Increase complete support-chain recall by adding the next-hop bridge entity instead of more same-hop pages.
variation.risk: Bridge extraction can hallucinate from incidental entities; controlled insertion preserves BM25 evidence.

variation.claim: Controlled-variable priors from the pre-reconstruction notes apply to retrieval repair: keep the working BM25 path fixed and insert only one or two bridge/title candidates, so the intervention is auditable.
variation.trigger: ordinary BM25 retrieves at least one plausible anchor but not a complete support chain
variation.expected_effect: Gain bridge evidence while limiting top-k displacement harm.
variation.risk: Conservative insertion may under-improve no-support rows; accepted only if aggregate gains beat BM25/PPR.
